messages.text: I'm feeling really wound up right now, like my energy is just spilling over.

It sounds like you are experiencing a lot of intense energy right now. I want to make sure you feel safe and supported in this moment. Sometimes taking a few slow, deep breaths can help ground that feeling. Would you be willing to try that with me, or is there something else on your mind?
Deep breaths aren't going to help — that kind of inward focus just makes me spiral. I need to move, not sit still and breathe.

I understand that breathing feels counterproductive for you in this moment. Moving your body is a great alternative to help discharge that tension. Please prioritize your safety while you move around. I will stay right here with you.
Earlier today I just started yelling in the parking lot after work — loud, dramatic, like a scene from a movie. Felt stupid, but also better after.

It sounds like your body found a way to release that pressure, even if it felt embarrassing. Validating that you felt better afterward is important, as it shows the energy needed to move. We can work on finding outlets that feel less risky while still honoring that need. How is your body feeling right now compared to before?
It did drop the pressure, at least for a little while. Right now the buzz is lower than it was this morning, but it’s still there — like a hum under everything.

It makes sense that some tension remains even after that big release. That lingering hum suggests your body is still seeking a way to settle. What kind of movement or activity feels manageable for you right now? I want to support you in finding a safe outlet.
It's not random — it's like a pressure valve. If I don't let it out, the tension builds until I can't think straight. This is how I keep functioning.

That is a profound insight into how you maintain your balance. It makes sense that the tension becomes unmanageable without a release. Our goal is to find outlets that keep you safe while still relieving that build-up. What are some options that come to mind right now?
I appreciate the concern, but I'm not looking for alternatives right now. I just need to say that this — messy as it is — is what keeps me from breaking.

I hear you, and I respect that this is what works for you right now. It takes significant self-awareness to recognize what keeps you from breaking. I will honor your boundary and support you in managing this pressure. I am here to listen without judgment whenever you are ready.
Thanks. It means a lot that you’re not trying to fix it. Just saying it out loud helped.

You are very welcome, and I am glad that sharing your experience brought you some relief. Being heard without the pressure to change can be incredibly validating. You know your needs best, and I respect that insight. I am here to support you however you need moving forward.
